scope: G3 functional branch only: test-only reconciliation, by a retry under a new original, of complete reserved first index job members that interrupted job selection attempts left in a real migrated V2 store, and synchronization of every reserved member before the selection's NV dispatch; an additive read-only content-store synchronization method; no production caller, produced image, GWIN0 package, installed run or native C activation

branch_policy.owner_decision: On 29 October 2026 the owner kept further sequence-19 G2 testing and GWIN0 completion on feature/g3-gwin0-beta and moved G3 functional development to this branch; on 31 October 2026 the owner approved the index job selection step in the words: may I add the step that turns the reserved first index job into the selected job, plus its reopen check? yes. This checkpoint closes the reconciliation item that the job selection checkpoint left open

implementation: An index job selection retry under a new original walks the actual v2 store and splits the walk into the C-reserved job members it shows and the object prefixes every other file already holds. The walk is measured data, never a recovery grant or permission to adopt a file

The walk is admitted only when it equals the C-selected owner accounting, or exceeds it only by complete C-reserved members: exact regular-file and logical-byte deltas, allocated bytes at least theirs, no more new directories than the reserved prefixes no other file holds, and an unchanged incomplete-object count. A partial member, a member of another length, a foreign object, a store behind C or any other difference is refused before any store write or NV dispatch
A reserved member that C already accounts for counts as new, so a store ahead of C over such a member is refused rather than guessed

The observed writer begins only when the actual store walk equals the admitted walk. The existing writer re-reads each present member byte for byte and writes only the missing ones; the measured after-state must still fit the reservation's liability, as before

luma-content-store gains an additive read-only ObjectStore::synchronize_objects. For an exact write set it reads each member from a held descriptor, checks its exact length and digest, synchronizes the file, both prefix directories and the object root, and rechecks the held identity. It never creates, adopts or selects anything; a missing, incomplete or differently sized member refuses, as do an empty set, write admission and a revoked boundary. Existing writer behaviour is unchanged

The closed direct worker's job selection calls it for every C-reserved member after the job blob read-back and before it measures the store and dispatches NV, because reuse through write_object only re-reads an existing member and the attempt that wrote it may have stopped before its own synchronization (ADR 0014: allocate, synchronize and read back all new content before any NV dispatch)

The reservation's own original still never selects. The selection event, its domain luma-c-index-job-selection-v1, the cold verifier and the single NV dispatch are unchanged from the job selection checkpoint

The publisher still has no production caller; production builds do not compile the direct publisher, its cold verifiers or the test-only variants. synchronize_objects is compiled into production builds and has no production caller
production_change: luma-content-store gains an additive read-only ObjectStore::synchronize_objects, compiled into production builds with no production caller; existing writer behaviour unchanged

test_behaviour: Each direct test first runs a real bounded owner migration into a real side-by-side v2 store, so Start, job selection and reconciliation run over the actual C-selected migrated V2 owner
The reconciliation test dispatches and cold-reopens one Start reservation; the reserved job blob has three members (one chunk, one group and the blob index), none of them in the store

A first interrupted attempt stops right after the first member's last write: that member is complete, nothing after it is written and there is no C event; the store is one regular file ahead of C with the incomplete-object count unchanged
A selection under the reservation's own original is refused before NV and before any store write, with the store inventory unchanged

The actual worker under a new original reuses the first member, writes the other two and is revoked right after the last: it is refused before NV, the store holds all three members, the blob reads back as the C-derived job bytes and a cold reopen still selects the reservation

A retry under another new original reconciles with exactly one NV dispatch and nothing more written; the blob still reads back, and a cold reopen selects the reconciled job selection with the same binding, input digest, selection and original attribution, sequence one higher and changed owner and index roots

The pure walk test admits exactly C, C plus the whole blob and its new directories, and C plus one member with or without directories made for the members never written; it refuses more directories than the free reserved prefixes, a store behind C, a lost allocation, a foreign object beside a member, foreign bytes, a foreign partial object, an incomplete member, a member of another length and a store ahead of C over a member C already accounts for

The content-store test synchronizes a stored member with the inventory unchanged, and refuses a set with an absent member (which is never created), another length, an empty set, write admission, a revoked boundary and a set with a retained interrupted partial object, which stays retained with the inventory unchanged
The Start test and the lost-reply Start test are unchanged from the job selection checkpoint and still pass

Platform unit tests ran serially; the parallel test interference stays open

not_claimed: Recovery of a partial member or a foreign object; a store holding one is refused before NV and the reservation's liability stays charged
Verification of the identities of objects C already accounts for; the walk compares counters, so a same-size swap of a C-accounted object is not detected by it
Re-synchronization by other v2 writers that reuse an existing object through write_object
Cold re-verification of the job blob or other object-store bytes; the cold verifier replays the C records and roots only
A power-loss, crash-consistency or page-cache-drop test of the synchronization; the tests use software interruption and revocation
The three rustfmt pre-checks of the working tree (D:/LumaOS-builds/g3-slice7-fmt-precheck-20261031-a, -b and -c); they are retained formatting aids, not gate checks
A cold lineage verifier for an index phase preparation; a cut over one is refused
A C reservation of the fresh v2 namespace or joined protected C counters
Running the selected job, any index phase preparation after it or a published index generation
A production index grant shape, a production caller, an installed run or native C activation
Reconciliation of an unselected pending worker attempt after a lost NV reply
Delta overlay, snapshot backup delivery or a V2 owner creation route
Artifact CLI harness passage, installed PAM, physical TPM, loaded LSM or Hyper-V qualification
Any produced image or GWIN0 package; G3 and GWIN0 remain open
